(a) Show that \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{2 y-x}\).

(c) Show that there are no points \((x, y)\) on the curve where the line tangent to the curve is horizontal.

\section*{Question 5}

Consider the curve given by \(y^{2}=2+x y\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Show that \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{2 y-x}\).
\item[(b)] Find all points \((x, y)\) on the curve where the line tangent to the curve has slope \(\frac{1}{2}\).
\item[(c)] Show that there are no points \((x, y)\) on the curve where the line tangent to the curve is horizontal.
\item[(d)] Let \(x\) and \(y\) be functions of time \(t\) that are related by the equation \(y^{2}=2+x y\). At time \(t=5\), the value of \(y\) is 3 and \(\frac{d y}{d t}=6\). Find the value of \(\frac{d x}{d t}\) at time \(t=5\).
\item[(a)] \(2 y y^{\prime}=y+x y^{\prime}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& (2 y-x) y^{\prime}=y \\
& y^{\prime}=\frac{y}{2 y-x}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(\frac{y}{2 y-x}=\frac{1}{2}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& 2 y=2 y-x \\
& x=0 \\
& y= \pm \sqrt{2} \\
& (0, \sqrt{2}),(0,-\sqrt{2})
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(\frac{y}{2 y-x}=0\)
\[
y=0
\]
The curve has no horizontal tangent since
\[
0^{2} \neq 2+x \cdot 0 \text { for any } x .
\]
\item[(d)] When \(y=3,3^{2}=2+3 x\) so \(x=\frac{7}{3}\).
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{d y}{d x} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{y}{2 y-x} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t} \\
& \text { At } t=5,6=\frac{3}{6-\frac{7}{3}} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{9}{11} \cdot \frac{d x}{d t} \\
& \left.\frac{d x}{d t}\right|_{t=5}=\frac{22}{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { implicit differentiation } \\ 1: \text { solves for } y^{\prime}\end{array}\right.\)
\begin{itemize}
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \frac{y}{2 y-x}=\frac{1}{2} \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: y=0 \\ 1: \text { explanation }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { solves for } x \\ 1: \text { chain rule } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\end{itemize}
